title: Tenanted warmup hysteresis causes reserved-pool shortfall during cross-region surge
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: A production escalation from a high-volume customer (AtlasPay) revealed a reserved-pool capacity shortfall during a multi-region traffic spike. The platform failed to surface burst capacity for several tenants for ~18 minutes, causing elevated 429s and sustained latency degradation for warm traffic. Preliminary investigation points to an interaction between tenant-level warmup hysteresis in the scale controller and a warm-run crediting bug that prevented recently-warmed slots and KV-cache priming from being accounted towards burst headroom. The combination led to systematic underestimation of available headroom when the autoscaler made multi-tenant slot decisions under a short-term surge.
impact: Customers in affected reserved pools experienced 429 throttles and tail latency regressions for ~18 minutes. AtlasPay reported payment processing retries and elevated error rates; customer impact classified as high. Several other mid-market customers saw transient SLO breaches. No data loss or security exposure detected.
timeline_summary: 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC - AtlasPay support alert; 09:18 UTC - paging; 09:22 UTC - mitigation (forced replenish) initiated; 09:40 UTC - short-term service recovery observed; 11:00 UTC - root-cause triage begins; 2026-03-11 - targeted hotfix rolled to Canary; 2026-03-13 - hotfix promoted to production for affected regions; ongoing verification through 2026-03-14.
repro_steps: Simulate a multi-region burst where tenant A increases qps by 6x within 30s and tenant B simultaneously performs warmup allocations.
Trigger autoscaler predictive window with default tenant-weighted hysteresis (30s smoothing) enabled.
Observe reserved-pool headroom accounting while warm-run crediting flag for KV cache priming is unset for dedicated pools (reproducer uses dev-kv-cache toggles).
Result: autoscaler underestimates headroom and denies burst slot allocations despite physical slots being available and partially warmed.
investigation_notes: Found a deviation in the scale-controller: tenant warmup hysteresis was implemented as a multiplicative smoothing over the predictive signal, which accumulates stale negative headroom when multiple small tenants warm simultaneously.

A separate codepath that credits warm-run/KV-cache readiness for hosted pools was not executed for Dedicated pool allocations due to an early return in alloc_decider() introduced in runtime-1.20. This meant partially-warmed slots were not counted toward immediate headroom.
Telemetry: headroom metric (reserved_pool_effective_headroom) diverged from physical_free_slots by ~40% during the incident; granularity gap in tenant-level warmup metrics made detection slower.
Hypothesis: the hysteresis smoothing amplified the missing warm-credit signal, causing the autoscaler to prefer conservative scheduling and trigger denials.
mitigation_taken: Force-replenish job started to temporarily inflate available headroom in affected pools (09:22 UTC).
Short-term config change: reduced tenant warmup hysteresis window from 30s -> 8s for Canary and affected regions to allow faster re-evaluation (09:30 UTC).
Hotfix PR (#2978) implemented to ensure warm-run/KV-cache crediting runs for Dedicated pool allocation codepath (merged 03-11).
Promoted hotfix to production for the three impacted regions with staged rollout (03-13).
Customer comms: support posted a detailed incident update to AtlasPay and published a summary on the status page.
proposed_long_term_actions: Add a new metric: tenant_warm_credit_ratio (per-tenant) and expose it in Console with alerts when ratio < 0.8.
Rewrite hysteresis to be additive with explicit decay and upper/lower bounds rather than multiplicative smoothing so it cannot amplify missing signals.
Introduce a post-allocation verification step that confirms warm-credit accounting has been applied; if not, auto-trigger a fast-path replenish and emit a diagnostic event.
End-to-end canary: create a synthetic workload that exercises cross-tenant multi-region bursts every week to detect regressions in headroom accounting.
Update runbooks and include decision-tree for forced replenish vs hotfix rollouts, and ownership for Customer Success comms.
customer_comm: Initial customer update acknowledging incident sent 2026-03-10 10:02 UTC. Follow-up technical write-up and mitigation timeline sent 2026-03-13 17:45 UTC. AtlasPay accepted the remediation plan and requested a post-incident review meeting.
